logp.method_description: The determination of the partition coefficients of target complexes using the classic n-octanol/water shake-flask method can be summarized as follows: First, equal volumes of n-octanol and purified water were mixed and shaken at 37°C for 24 h to allow mutual saturation of the two phases. After standing for 1 h, the phases were separated for later use. The complexes were dissolved in water-saturated n-octanol to prepare solutions at concentrations of 40, 60, 80, 100, and 120 μM. The absorbance of each concentration was measured in triplicate using a UV–Vis spectrophotometer, and the average values were used to construct a standard curve to ensure reliable linearity. Subsequently, n-octanol-saturated aqueous solution was placed in a centrifuge tube, and the target complex was added to prepare a 50 μM test sample. The mixture was shaken at 37°C for 48 h to ensure equilibrium distribution. After standing for 1 h, the phases were completely separated by centrifugation at 2500 rpm for 15 min. The solutions from both phases were sampled using syringes, and their absorbance values were measured in triplicate using a UV–Vis spectrophotometer. The average values were used for subsequent concentration calculations. The lipid phase concentration (Co) was calculated based on the standard curve, and the aqueous phase concentration (Cw) was determined using the principle of mass conservation. The LogPo/w of the complex was calculated using Equation (1): log Po/w = log(Co / Cw)

After mixing octanol and purified water in a 15-mL centrifuge tube, the mixture was shaken in a constant temperature shaker at 37°C for 24 h to achieve mutual saturation of the two phases, preparing saturated solutions of both phases. After allowing the solution to settle for 1 h, it was separated and kept aside. The complexes were dissolved in water-saturated octanol to obtain solutions of 40, 60, 80, 100, and 120 μM concentrations. UV/Vis absorbance measurements were used to construct a standard curve. Subsequently, using the octanol-saturated solution prepared earlier as the solvent, a 50 μM test sample was prepared. An equal volume of water-saturated solution was added, and the mixture was oscillated at 37°C for 48 h. Afterward, the mixed solution was centrifuged at 2500 rpm for 15 min to separate the two phases. The absorbance of the octanol solution was measured using a UV spectrophotometer, and the drug's concentration in the octanol phase (Co) was calculated using the standard curve. According to the principle of mass conservation, the concentration in the water phase (Cw) was determined, and log Po/w was calculated by Formula (1). Log Po/w = log(Co/Cw)
